title: Importer v2: category mapping and atomic batches
pr_description: Statement import learns two things users kept asking for: map merchant descriptions to categories (case-insensitive prefix rules, e.g. 'COFFEE' -> food), and all-or-nothing batches so a bad row no longer leaves a half-imported statement. Duplicate detection was also simplified and sped up by keying on (date, amount).

defects.description: Deduplication now keys on (date, amount) only — the description was dropped from the check. Two different merchants charging the same amount on the same day (two $9.99 subscriptions) means the second is silently skipped as a 'duplicate'. Data loss relative to v1, which included the note.

The description is uppercased but the user-supplied mapping prefix is used as-given, so any mapping rule not written in ALL CAPS ('Coffee' -> food) never matches and the docstring's 'case-insensitive' promise is false. Both sides must be normalized.

The batch is wrapped in db.transaction(), but every add_expense call goes through db.execute, which runs its own transaction and COMMITs immediately (see db.py). A failure mid-batch still leaves earlier rows committed — the advertised all-or-nothing behavior does not exist.

The test named test_atomic_batch imports an all-valid statement and asserts success. It never includes a failing row, so it cannot detect that atomicity is broken — the one scenario it is named after.
